title: PRAgent: AI-Assisted Physics Paper Reproduction
subtitle: Capabilities and Evidence from a 100-Paper Project
comments: Technical report, 10 pages, 5 main figures and a supplementary cohort figure. Code and public research artifacts: https://github.com/xi-zhao/RunThePaper
abstract: Reproducing a physics paper requires an executable interpretation of its model, a suitable numerical method and checks that connect the computed observables to the scientific question. We present PRAgent, an AI-assisted system that brings these tasks together in a human-guided research workflow. We examine its implemented capabilities through three public research cases: precision-aware evaluation of Hamiltonian-simulation resource bounds, quantum dynamics in exact particle-number sectors, and ensemble-based quantum-discord calculations. The cases show how physical structure determines the computational representation, how numerical difficulties are handled in code, and how controls and statistical comparisons constrain the interpretation of results. A fixed 100-paper project provides a broader view of recorded reproduction coverage and verification status. Further diagnostic examples examine source ambiguity, incomplete model implementations and resource requirements. Our evidence consists of case-specific implementations, archived computational outputs and new checks of selected stored arrays. It supports an account of PRAgent's demonstrated capabilities within the recorded human-guided workflow. RunThePaper makes the resulting code, data and explanations available as research artifacts that can be inspected and extended.
